meta.purpose: Forensic accounting anomaly signatures used by the deterministic generator (injection magnitudes) and by the pedagogy layer (detection paths). Magnitudes are ranges observed in enforcement actions and the cited literature; the generator scales them by difficulty.
primary_sources: Schilit, Perler & Engelhart, Financial Shenanigans, 4th ed., McGraw-Hill 2018
Beneish, M. D. (1999). The Detection of Earnings Manipulation. Financial Analysts Journal 55(5), 24-36
Sloan, R. G. (1996). Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows about Future Earnings? The Accounting Review 71(3), 289-315
ACFE, Occupational Fraud 2024: A Report to the Nations
Nigrini, M. J. (2012). Benford's Law: Applications for Forensic Accounting, Auditing, and Fraud Detection. Wiley
SEC Accounting and Auditing Enforcement Releases (AAER) as cited per pattern

patterns.title: Channel stuffing
patterns.description: Pushing more product into the distribution channel than end demand supports near period end, often with extended terms, deep discounts or return rights, so revenue is recognized before economic sale to end customers.
signatures: Revenue in the last 5 business days of the quarter rises from ~10-14% to 25-40% of quarterly revenue
DSO rises while revenue growth accelerates; receivables grow faster than revenue (Beneish DSRI > 1.2)
Concentration: the increase sits in a handful of distributors
Terms on quarter-end invoices extended (net 90-120 vs net 30-45) and discounts 5-12 points higher
Returns in the following period 2.5-4x baseline for the window orders; next-quarter orders from the same accounts drop 50-80% of the stuffed amount
CFO lags net income; allowance for doubtful accounts held flat as AR grows

ratios: revenue last-5-day share vs history (window LAG over quarters)
returns rate for window vs non-window orders
detection.sql_sketch: SELECT q, SUM(amount) rev, SUM(CASE WHEN invoice_date >= quarter_end - 6 THEN amount END)/SUM(amount) last5_share, LAG(...) OVER (ORDER BY q) FROM invoices GROUP BY q
detection.python_sketch: window = inv[inv.days_to_qend <= 5]; two-sample test of return rates window vs rest; distributor concentration (HHI) by quarter

patterns.title: Bill-and-hold revenue
patterns.description: Invoicing and recognizing revenue for goods not yet shipped, with the goods held by the seller, where ASC 606 bill-and-hold criteria (customer-requested, substantive reason, goods identified and ready, seller cannot redirect) are not met.
signatures: Invoices with ship_date after period end or NULL; shipment status 'awaiting release'
Gross margin spikes in the period (revenue booked, COGS at shipment) then reverses
Inventory sub-ledger shows no issue for invoiced units
Hold request notes originate from seller, not customer

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT SUM(i.amount) FROM invoices i JOIN orders o USING(order_id) LEFT JOIN shipments s USING(order_id) WHERE s.ship_date IS NULL OR s.ship_date > period_end(i.invoice_date)
detection.python_sketch: merge invoices/shipments; flag ship_date > period_end; margin by period with/without flagged rows

real_cases.name: Diebold

patterns.title: Premature / cutoff revenue recognition
patterns.description: Recognizing revenue before performance obligations are satisfied: cutoff errors at period end, recognizing on signing rather than delivery, or recognizing multi-period subscriptions up front.
signatures: Invoice dates clustered in the last 2-3 days of the period with delivery in the first days of the next
Deferred revenue falls relative to billings for subscription businesses
Unbilled receivables / contract assets rise faster than revenue
Revenue per customer jumps in Q4 and falls in Q1

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT invoice_date, ship_date FROM invoices JOIN shipments USING(order_id) WHERE date_trunc('quarter', invoice_date) <> date_trunc('quarter', ship_date)
detection.python_sketch: histogram of revenue by day-of-quarter; compare deferred revenue roll-forward to billings

patterns.title: Round-trip transactions
patterns.description: Selling to and buying from the same counterparty (or an affiliate) in offsetting transactions to fabricate revenue with little or no economic substance.
signatures: A supplier and a customer share tax id, address, bank account or officers (fuzzy matches after normalizing case/whitespace)
Sales to the customer roughly equal purchases from the supplier in the same month
Margin on those sales near zero; cash often never moves (netting)
Revenue growth without commensurate cash flow or inventory movement

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT c.customer_id, s.supplier_id FROM customers c JOIN suppliers s ON lower(trim(c.tax_id)) = lower(trim(s.tax_id)) OR lower(trim(c.address)) = lower(trim(s.address))
detection.python_sketch: fuzzy entity resolution (rapidfuzz) across customers/suppliers; monthly net flows by matched pair

patterns.title: Capitalizing operating expenses
patterns.description: Recording ordinary operating costs (line costs, marketing, maintenance, R&D) as assets to spread them over future periods and inflate current earnings.
signatures: Capitalized software / other assets grow much faster than revenue
Capex % revenue jumps without a stated program; FCF (CFO - capex) deteriorates while CFO looks fine
Engineering payroll share capitalized rises from ~20% to 50%+
Depreciation/amortization lag: D&A / gross assets falls

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT period, SUM(CASE WHEN account='1600' THEN debit END)/SUM(CASE WHEN dept='engineering' THEN payroll END) FROM ...
detection.python_sketch: recompute EBITDA with capitalized amounts expensed; compare margin paths

real_cases.summary: ~$3.8B of line costs capitalized as assets (ultimately $11B restatement).

sources: Schilit ch. 5 (Shifting current expenses to a later period)

patterns.title: Cookie-jar reserves
patterns.description: Over-accruing reserves (restructuring, warranty, returns, bad debt) in good periods and releasing them in weak periods to smooth earnings.
signatures: Reserve balances as % of the driver (sales, AR) oscillate counter-cyclically with earnings misses
Large reserve builds coincide with 'big bath' restructuring; subsequent releases flow through operating income
Journal entries to reserve accounts cluster at quarter end, manual, round amounts

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT period, SUM(credit-debit) reserve_activity, is_manual, amount % 10000 = 0 AS round FROM gl_lines WHERE account IN ('1110','2450','2100') GROUP BY ...
detection.python_sketch: regress reserve changes on earnings surprise; flag negative correlation

patterns.title: Phantom / overstated inventory
patterns.description: Inventory that does not exist or is worth less than carried, overstating assets and understating COGS.
signatures: Inventory grows faster than COGS (DIO rising) with gross margin improving
Cycle-count adjustments trend negative and are reversed at period end
Inventory roll-forward (begin + purchases - COGS) does not tie to the sub-ledger
Obsolete / slow-moving SKUs with no write-down

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT sku, SUM(qty_in)-SUM(qty_out) book_qty, last_count_qty FROM inventory_movements ... JOIN inventory_counts
detection.python_sketch: roll-forward test per SKU; aging of inventory by last sale date

patterns.title: Understated allowance for doubtful accounts
patterns.description: Holding the bad-debt allowance flat or reducing it while receivables age and grow, boosting earnings.
signatures: Allowance % of AR declines while AR aging (90+) grows
Bad debt expense % revenue declines
Write-offs exceed provisions for several periods (allowance draw-down)

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT period, SUM(CASE WHEN days_past_due > 90 THEN open END) over90, allowance FROM aging JOIN tb ...
detection.python_sketch: expected loss = Σ bucket × historical loss rate; compare to allowance

patterns.title: Stretched payables / supplier financing masking cash burn
patterns.description: Delaying vendor payments or using reverse-factoring to inflate CFO; the liability may be reclassified out of AP.
signatures: DPO rises 10-30 days over 2-4 quarters; CFO improvement equals ΔAP
Suppliers tighten terms, put accounts on hold, or demand prepayment; stockouts follow
Supplier-finance programs disclosed vaguely; AP 'other' grows

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT period, AVG(paid_at - bill_date) days_to_pay, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status='on_hold') FROM vendor_bills ...
detection.python_sketch: CFO ex-ΔAP series; supplier-level payment lag drift

patterns.title: Related-party sales
patterns.description: Revenue from entities controlled by insiders, often on non-market terms, with collectability and substance in doubt.
signatures: Customers sharing addresses/officers with the company or its executives
Unusually long or unpaid receivables from those customers
Sales concentrated at quarter end with high margins

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE address IN (SELECT address FROM officers) OR registered_agent = ...
detection.python_sketch: entity resolution customers × officer/affiliate list; collections performance subset

patterns.title: Period cutoff manipulation
patterns.description: Keeping the sales ledger open after period end or closing the purchase ledger early, shifting revenue earlier and expenses later.
signatures: GL posting dates after period end with document dates within the period (or vice versa)
Expense invoices dated in the period but posted in the next (expenses deferred)
Shipping log dates vs invoice dates mismatch at the boundary

ratios: posting lag distribution at period end vs mid-period
detection.sql_sketch: SELECT j.entry_id FROM gl_journal j WHERE date_trunc('quarter', j.date) <> date_trunc('quarter', j.document_date)
detection.python_sketch: posting_lag = post_date - doc_date; compare distribution for last 3 days vs rest

patterns.title: Unbilled receivables / contract assets growth
patterns.description: Revenue recognized on percentage-of-completion or usage without customer acceptance or invoicing, building contract assets that may not convert to cash.
signatures: Unbilled AR grows faster than billed AR and revenue
Unbilled / total AR rises above 25-30%
Large year-end unbilled reversed in Q1

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT period, SUM(unbilled) / SUM(total_ar) FROM ar_balances GROUP BY period
detection.python_sketch: conversion analysis: unbilled at t vs invoiced by t+90

patterns.title: Deferred revenue drawdown
patterns.description: Deferred revenue declines relative to recognized revenue, signalling slowing bookings or accelerated recognition; often masked by acquisitions or policy changes.
signatures: Deferred revenue / TTM revenue falls for 2+ quarters while revenue grows
Billings (revenue + Δdeferred) grow slower than revenue
Change in recognition policy (e.g., term shortening) disclosed as 'alignment'

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT period, revenue + (deferred_end - deferred_begin) billings FROM ...
detection.python_sketch: billings vs revenue growth series; policy change dummy

patterns.title: Sloan accrual ratio
patterns.description: High accruals (earnings not backed by cash flow) predict lower future earnings and returns. Accrual ratio = (Net income - CFO) / average total assets; or balance-sheet version (ΔNOA / avg NOA).
signatures: Accrual ratio > +10% of average assets
NI growing while CFO flat or falling for 2+ quarters

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT period, (net_income - cfo) / ((assets_begin + assets_end)/2.0) FROM statements

real_cases.name: Sloan (1996) sample
real_cases.summary: Hedge portfolio long low-accrual, short high-accrual earned ~10%/yr abnormal returns 1962-1991.

patterns.title: Beneish M-score (8-variable)
patterns.description: Probit model scoring the likelihood of earnings manipulation from year-over-year indices. M = -4.84 + 0.920*DSRI + 0.528*GMI + 0.404*AQI + 0.892*SGI + 0.115*DEPI - 0.172*SGAI + 4.679*TATA - 0.327*LVGI. M > -1.78 flags likely manipulation (Beneish 1999 cutoff; -2.22 in some later usage).
signatures: DSRI (Days Sales in Receivables Index) = (AR_t/Sales_t)/(AR_{t-1}/Sales_{t-1})
GMI (Gross Margin Index) = GM_{t-1}/GM_t
AQI (Asset Quality Index) = [1-(CA_t+PPE_t)/TA_t]/[1-(CA_{t-1}+PPE_{t-1})/TA_{t-1}]
SGI (Sales Growth Index) = Sales_t/Sales_{t-1}
DEPI (Depreciation Index) = [Dep_{t-1}/(Dep_{t-1}+PPE_{t-1})]/[Dep_t/(Dep_t+PPE_t)]
SGAI (SG&A Index) = (SGA_t/Sales_t)/(SGA_{t-1}/Sales_{t-1})
TATA (Total Accruals to Total Assets) = (Income from continuing ops - CFO)/TA_t
LVGI (Leverage Index) = [(LTD_t+CL_t)/TA_t]/[(LTD_{t-1}+CL_{t-1})/TA_{t-1}]

ratios: all eight indices on TTM vs prior TTM
detection.sql_sketch: compute TTM sums per period from statements; indices as ratios of consecutive TTM windows

patterns.title: Benford's Law first-digit test
patterns.description: Naturally occurring transaction amounts follow P(d) = log10(1 + 1/d) for the first digit; fabricated or rounded amounts deviate. Applies to data spanning several orders of magnitude without imposed limits.
signatures: Excess of first digits 5-9 (invented numbers) or spikes at specific digits (threshold gaming, e.g., many 4,9xx amounts below a 5,000 approval limit)
Mean absolute deviation (MAD) > 0.015 for first digit (Nigrini 'nonconformity')
Round-number share (amount % 100 == 0) far above the ~3-8% typical for invoices

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT substr(cast(amount_cents/100 as varchar),1,1) d, COUNT(*)*1.0/SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () FROM invoices WHERE amount_cents >= 1000 GROUP BY 1
detection.python_sketch: obs = first_digit_counts/n; exp = np.log10(1+1/np.arange(1,10)); mad = np.abs(obs-exp).mean(); chi2 test

patterns.title: Journal entry red flags (AS 2401 / SAS 99 tests)
patterns.description: Top-side and manual entries that bypass normal processing are the primary vehicle for management override. Standard tests examine timing, amounts, preparers and accounts.
signatures: Manual entries posted in the last 3 days of the period or after close (post-closing)
Round amounts (multiples of 1,000 / 10,000) and amounts just under approval thresholds
Entries posted on weekends/holidays or outside business hours
Preparer is senior (CFO/controller) or a non-accounting user; same person prepares and approves
Entries to seldom-used or suspense accounts; entries with blank or generic descriptions ('adj', 'per CFO')
Reversals shortly after period end

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT preparer, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE source='manual' AND (date >= period_end - 2 OR dayofweek(date) IN (0,6) OR amount % 100000 = 0)) FROM gl_journal GROUP BY 1
detection.python_sketch: score each JE on 6 flags; rank; sample for substantive review

real_cases.summary: Top-side entries by senior finance staff moved line costs to capital accounts.

patterns.title: Duplicate vendor payments
patterns.description: Paying the same invoice twice through re-keyed invoice numbers, vendor duplicates, or system re-runs; a recovery-audit staple and a control weakness indicator.
signatures: Same vendor, same amount, within 30 days; invoice numbers differing by punctuation/case/leading zeros
Same amount to two vendor ids with similar names/addresses/bank accounts
Payment runs re-executed after a job failure

detection.sql_sketch: SELECT a.payment_id, b.payment_id FROM payments a JOIN payments b ON a.vendor_id=b.vendor_id AND a.amount=b.amount AND a.payment_id<b.payment_id AND abs(datediff('day',a.paid_at,b.paid_at))<=30 AND regexp_replace(lower(a.invoice_no),'[^a-z0-9]','')=regexp_replace(lower(b.invoice_no),'[^a-z0-9]','')
detection.python_sketch: normalize invoice numbers; fuzzy vendor matching; pairwise within window

real_cases.name: Medicare duplicate payments (OIG)
real_cases.summary: OIG audits routinely find duplicate claims paid; e.g., $3.3M duplicate payments for selected services.

sources: ACFE Report to the Nations (billing schemes)

patterns.title: Ghost / shell vendors
patterns.description: Fictitious vendors created by an insider to route payments; the most common billing-scheme fraud per ACFE.
signatures: Vendor address or bank account matches an employee's
Vendor created and first paid within days; no PO, no receiving record; round amounts just under approval limit
P.O. box address; no tax id; sequential invoice numbers (only customer is you)
Payments approved by the same user who created the vendor

ratios: vendor master vs employee master match rate
detection.sql_sketch: SELECT v.vendor_id FROM vendors v JOIN employees e ON v.bank_account=e.bank_account OR lower(trim(v.address))=lower(trim(e.address))
detection.python_sketch: Benford on vendor amounts; invoice-number gap analysis per vendor; created_by == approved_by
